problem_motivation.content: The system tends to decompose into a two-phase mixture when Co is substituted with Cr or at lower annealing temperatures, creating a need to understand and control this behavior.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: both the substitution of ferromagnetic Co with antiferromagnetic Cr, and lower annealing temperatures lead to a tendency for this system to decompose into a two-phase mixture

problem_motivation.content: Limited knowledge exists regarding the composition and temperature dependent microstructure and properties in the AlCoCrFeNi system, necessitating further investigation into the role of Cr.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: there is rather limited knowledge regarding the composition and temperature dependent microstructure and properties in the AlCo x Cr 1−x FeNi system [13] . Therefore, the role of Cr, an anti-ferromagnetic element, on the microstructural evolution and properties (magnetic and mechanical) of AlCo x Cr 1−x FeNi type HEAs, needs further investigation and forms the basis of the present study.

prior_approach.content: Previous studies have reported on the microstructure of AlCoCrFeNi based HEAs under various processing conditions, including graded samples and annealing treatments.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Recently, it has been reported that AlCoCrFeNi based HEAs exhibit high hardness, good corrosion resistance, high yield strength and promising magnetic properties [1] , [11] – [15] . A systematic investigation on a compositionally graded AlCo x Cr 1− x FeNi sample, processed by laser engineered net shape (LENS) technology [13] , revealed that all the compositions within this graded sample exhibited either a single B2 phase or a two-phase BCC + B2 microstructure. A separate study reported that annealing the AlCoCrFeNi HEA at 600 °C, exhibited a near single B2 phase microstructure, while the same alloy annealed in the temperature range of 800 to 1200 °C exhibited FCC precipitates in a B2 matrix [15] .

prior_approach.content: Extensive investigation has been conducted on the influence of Al content in the AlxCoCrFeNi class of HEAs.
prior_approach.evidence_span: While the influence of Al content on the phases and microstructures, in the Al x CoCrFeNi class of HEAs has been extensively investigated [10] , [16] , [17] ,

mechanism_principle.content: The enhanced phase separation tendency in Cr-containing alloys is attributed to positive enthalpy of mixing in Fe-Cr, Co-Cr, and Ni-Cr systems.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The strong tendency of Cr to introduce phase separation in the B2 phase can possibly be attributed to a positive enthalpy of mixing of Fe-Cr, Co-Cr and Ni-Cr systems [37] , leading to miscibility gaps observed in these binary systems and a tendency for phase separation.

evidence_result.content: Replacing Co with Cr substantially reduced saturation magnetization while increasing coercivity.
evidence_result.evidence_span: replacement of Co by Cr in the AlCoFeNi alloy resulted in a substantial reduction in saturation magnetization and increase in coercivity

evidence_result.content: Microhardness is strongly affected by alloy composition and the length scale of the B2 + BCC decomposition.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The microhardness is also strongly influenced by the composition and the length scale of B2 + BCC decomposition in these high entropy alloys

evidence_result.content: Annealing AlCoFeNi at 1000°C for 15h results in a single-phase B2 microstructure.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Thus, these AlCoFeNi samples consist of a single phase with a B2 crystal structure.

evidence_result.content: Annealing AlCoFeNi at 600°C for 15h results in a two-phase microstructure with an Al-Ni rich B2 matrix and Fe-Co rich BCC precipitates.
evidence_result.evidence_span: From the APT and TEM results, the two phases can be characterized as the Al-Ni rich B2 matrix interspersed with fine scale precipitates of a Fe-Co rich BCC phase.

evidence_result.content: Partial replacement of Co with Cr induces strong phase separation in AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi at both 600°C and 1000°C.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Hence, addition of Cr to AlCoFeNi substantially changes the microstructure by introducing a strong tendency of phase separation in the B2 phase to form a two-phase mixture.

evidence_result.content: High-resolution TEM confirms lattice continuity (coherency) between the B2 and BCC phases in the Cr-containing alloy.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The high-resolution TEM image shown in Fig. 6(e) clearly reveals the continuity of the BCC lattice between the ordered B2 and disordered BCC phases.

evidence_result.content: Microhardness is lower for single-phase B2 AlCoFeNi at 1000°C compared to multi-scale decomposed AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi at 600°C.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Consequently, the single phase B2 microstructure has a lower hardness as compared to the hierarchically decomposed B2 + BCC microstructure.

evidence_result.content: Coercivity decreases as annealing temperature increases and phase separation diminishes.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The coercivity ( H c ) decreased with increasing annealing temperature from 15 Oe for sample aged at 600 °C/15 h, exhibiting nanoscale phase separation, to 4 Oe for samples aged at 1000 °C/15 h, exhibiting a homogeneous undecomposed B2 matrix.
